headline: North Korea says it has tested a new torpedo, called Zam-2.0, that uses artificial intelligence to detect targets and steer the weapon.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a state-media claim that is unexplained and unverified, but part of a run of North Korean naval weapons tests.
importance_line: People in South Korea and Japan and their governments face a North Korea that is shifting its focus to naval weapons, but the AI claim comes only from state media, is unexplained and is doubted by some experts.
summary: The Associated Press reports that North Korea's state news agency KCNA said on 17 Oct 2026 that it tested the "super-speed, precisely guided" Zam-2.0 torpedo system on 15 Oct 2026, and that the test verified propulsion systems developed over more than 180 tests in five years. KCNA did not explain what it meant by artificial intelligence, South Korea's military did not immediately comment, and AP notes that some experts doubt the country's weapons really have advanced digital abilities such as choosing targets on their own.
notes: AP original returned HTTP 403; text read in The Hindu copy, which carries the AP headline (no AP credit printed on the extracted page), cross-checked with Euronews. The test (15 Oct) is before 16 Oct but the claim first became public on 17 Oct, so freshness is NEW. machine_action false: a weapon test claimed by state media, not shown by independent evidence.
